tower-of-hanoi.title: Move largest disk first if not on target
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the largest remaining disk is not already on its goal peg and there are no smaller disks on top of it, move it directly to its target peg. Without this, you may attempt to move a larger disk while a smaller one blocks it, causing an illegal move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest disk is free (no smaller disks above) and not yet at its goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while a smaller disk sits on top, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve subproblem after moving largest disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After placing the largest disk on its goal peg, treat the remaining n‑1 disks as a new Tower of Hanoi problem and solve it recursively. Without this, you may continue moving disks without reducing the problem size, leading to a tangled state.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Once the largest disk is correctly placed and no smaller disks are above it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Continuing to move disks without focusing on the sub‑tower after the largest disk is fixed, leading to a tangled configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive move sequence for k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use the classic recursive algorithm: move k‑1 disks from source to auxiliary, move the kth disk to target, then move k‑1 disks from auxiliary to target. Without this, you may miss the optimal sequence and produce illegal placements.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When all disks start stacked on a single source peg and need to be moved to a target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disks without following the recursive pattern, resulting in illegal placements.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as final parseable output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the last parseable list of moves in the response is the complete solution, because the verifier extracts the final list. Without this, the verifier may read an earlier incomplete list and reject the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When outputting the solution, place the full move list as the very last parseable list in the response.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including additional text or another list after the move list, causing the verifier to ignore the correct solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, mentally simulate each move from the initial state to ensure the final configuration matches the goal. Without this, you may produce a move list that ends in an incorrect state.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the move list, run through the moves step‑by‑step to confirm the goal is reached.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves some disks on the wrong peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Concise final move list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep the reasoning brief and place only the complete move list as the final element of the response. Without this, extra text may be parsed incorrectly by the verifier.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the answer, ensure the only parseable list at the end is the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory text after the move list, causing the verifier to mis‑parse the solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When adding a move, check that the disk being moved is currently the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or has a larger top disk. Without this, you may attempt illegal moves that violate the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move list, before committing each move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, violating the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative smallest-disk cyclic algorithm
tower-of-hanoi.principle: For any Tower of Hanoi problem, repeatedly move the smallest disk to the next peg in a fixed direction (clockwise for odd number of disks, anticlockwise for even) and then make the only other legal move. Continue this pattern until the goal configuration is reached. This systematic approach guarantees legal moves and avoids getting stuck.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Applicable to any three‑peg Tower of Hanoi puzzle, regardless of initial distribution, when a deterministic solution is needed.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Choosing arbitrary moves without following a systematic pattern, leading to incomplete or illegal sequences.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or forget to output the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a non‑empty move list as the final parseable output.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops before listing all moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the solution to fit within token limits and ensure the full move list is output before ending.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of the current state while constructing moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Simulate each move mentally or on paper, checking that the moved disk is the topmost.
